<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }

  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents
<br class="ltx_break">as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Mobile GUI agents are typically fine-tuned 7B-scale vision-language models (VLMs) that generate each action as text.
However, these VLMs decode every action token by token, and even agents that score candidate actions keep a large language model or VLM in the loop, making them slow and memory-hungry.
To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots.
Its action- and region-conditioned latent predictor turns the screen latent into one latent per candidate action, letting lightweight heads score all candidates against the instruction in a single batched pass, without decoding a token.
We further show that the scorer relies on this latent pathway and that the predictor is trained for the decision itself: a randomly initialised predictor does just as well as one pretrained on screen dynamics.
On AndroidControl, GUI-JEPA is 2.8–4.0<math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster on the same GPU than a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent we fine-tune with the same inputs, while reaching 86–92% of its in-distribution accuracy with 6% of its parameters.
Code is available at <a href="https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA</a>.</p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para ltx_align_bottom">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center" style="width:345.0pt;"><span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"></span></p>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.36877v1/fig_hero.svg" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/314;" width="476" height="314"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Same inputs, same GPU: GUI-JEPA reaches 86–92% of the 7B agent’s accuracy at a fraction of its cost.</span> Bars are relative to our same-protocol Qwen2.5-VL-7B SFT agent, fine-tuned with LoRA (IDD AC-Low / AC-High accuracy; latency: medians over 100 shared real AC-High steps on one H20 at batch 1; peak memory under HF serving; <a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A mobile graphical user interface (GUI) agent’s per-step cost is dominated by a 7B+ vision-language model (VLM) decoding its action token by token. On one NVIDIA H20, a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> LoRA-fine-tuned <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> on AndroidControl needs 207 ms per step under vLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and 507 ms under Hugging Face (HF) transformers to emit a JSON action of <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}</annotation></semantics></math>12 tokens (median over 100 real steps, batch 1; <a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), and 8B-class agents average <span id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">2.6–10.6 s</span> per step in a live-device benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sui et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Yet in GUI grounding a VLM fixes its target elements during prefill, with decoding only refining coordinates <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>, and decoding on the critical path makes agents correct but late <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dong et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. Could a GUI agent <em id="S1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">score</em> its actions in the latent space of a joint-embedding predictive architecture <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2023</a>, JEPA;)</cite>, without decoding them at all?</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">GUI world models generate pixels, code or text and serve an LLM policy as simulator or verifier <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mei et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>, or as a pretraining target <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>. On GUIs, JEPAs have so far served understanding and verification: UI-JEPA describes user intent through an LLM decoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, LGWM verifies GUI transitions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>, and next-frame feature prediction regularises the training of a VLM agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>. Candidate scorers over the accessibility tree (a11y) keep an LLM or VLM in the loop <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang, 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christianos et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and Agentic-JEPA, which acts with a JEPA, is text-only with 0% out-of-distribution (OOD) success <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rodrigo-Ginés, 2026</a>)</cite>. To our knowledge, no GUI agent has yet used a JEPA as the policy that selects its actions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We bring JEPAs from perception and robotics to GUI control, moving action selection from the decoder into the latent space of a frozen JEPA encoder. GUI-JEPA encodes the screenshot once with a JEPA ViT-L pretrained on GUI screenshots, transforms that latent once per candidate (a11y element or global action) with a 39.9M residual predictor conditioned on the candidate’s action and region of interest (ROI), scores the candidate-conditioned latents with a cosine structural head, adds a 33M text-matcher score and takes the argmax, all in one batched pass (<a href="#S1.F2" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). As in earlier candidate-scoring agents, the candidates come from the a11y tree, but GUI-JEPA never generates a token, so the cost of a step depends on how many candidates it scores.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Under the same inputs, judge and GPU as a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent that we fine-tune with LoRA (SFT), GUI-JEPA is 2.8–4.0<math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster and reaches 92.4% / 86.1% of its in-distribution (IDD) Low / High accuracy with 6.0% of its parameters and 4.6–6.4<math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> less GPU memory (<a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Our contributions are:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GUI-JEPA</span>, the first GUI agent whose policy is built on a JEPA. It selects actions by scoring candidate-conditioned JEPA latents, with no decoder, and is <span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">2.8–4.0<math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math></span> faster than a same-protocol 7B agent that decodes token by token.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adapting a JEPA policy to GUIs:</span> a11y candidates as actions, ROI- and action-conditioned residual prediction, a structural head whose only candidate-dependent visual input is the conditioned latent, and two text rankers that together add 3.8 out-of-distribution AC-High points (<a href="#S4.T2" title="In 4.4 Gains from the two text rankers ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mechanism:</span> the scorer relies on the JEPA latent pathway, which is trained for the decision. A randomly initialised predictor matches a dynamics-pretrained one, so a JEPA policy for GUIs needs no dynamics pretraining.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.36877v1/fig_arch.png" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/210;" width="476" height="210" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span><span id="S1.F2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Overview of GUI-JEPA.</span> Top: on a real AndroidControl step, the frozen JEPA encoder embeds the screenshot once, the residual predictor turns it into one latent per candidate in a single batch, and the structural head and the text matcher score every candidate (bars: a trained base policy’s probabilities on this step; grids are schematic). Bottom: the training stages, and scoring in one pass versus decoding token by token (measured in <a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>). Circled numbers mark the stage that trains each module (1: JEPA pretraining, 2: policy training, 3: text rankers on the fixed policy); flame = trained, snowflake = frozen; green marks the recorded (correct) action.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">VLM GUI agents and their cost.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The dominant mobile GUI agent is a VLM of 7B+ parameters that emits an action token by token from a screenshot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qin et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite>; 3B agents report AndroidControl under incompatible protocols (<a href="#A6.T11" title="In Appendix F Other-protocol baselines ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>). On-device agents need seconds per step <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Park et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and efficiency work cheapens the decoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>; GUI-JEPA removes it altogether.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discriminative and candidate-scoring GUI agents.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Closest in input are the a11y-text PaLM 2S baselines of AndroidControl (<a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Main results ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>). LiMAC selects UI elements from screenshots and UI trees with a small action transformer, calls Florence-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> for text arguments and reports its own metric <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christianos et al., 2025</a>)</cite>; V-Droid verifies a11y candidates with a prefill-only LLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, Jev-Mobile selects a11y identifiers with a typed decision model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang, 2026</a>)</cite>, and IntentScore verifies a generative policy’s actions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>)</cite>; each keeps a generative LLM or VLM in the loop. GUI-JEPA shares a11y enumeration and argmax but scores a candidate-conditioned JEPA latent plus a 33M text matcher, with no generative model in the loop.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">World models for GUI agents.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GUI world models predict the next state as pixels <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ning et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, code <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>, text <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chae et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mei et al., 2026</a>)</cite> or textual element sketches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and serve an LLM policy as simulator, verifier or data synthesiser; none of the four output modalities compared by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al. (2026b)</a></cite> is joint-embedding. STP pretrains forward and inverse GUI dynamics in a unified multimodal model that still decodes actions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2026)</a></cite> train a generative text world model over a11y-tree states by predicted-state matching, whose predictions feed a separate reward model that ranks candidate actions. GUI-JEPA is decoder-free and <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">is</em> the policy, trained, like that web world model, for how it is used.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">JEPA and latent world models as policies.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In robotics, latent world models built on joint-embedding predictive architectures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2025</a>)</cite> plan <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maes et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zholus et al., 2026</a>)</cite> or drive action policies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2026b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>. On GUIs, UI-JEPA feeds a JEPA-pretrained video encoder into a fine-tuned LLM decoder that describes user intent, with a reported 6.6<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> lower latency than Claude 3.5 Sonnet on IIW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>; the concurrent LGWM, a JEPA over GUI transitions, verifies whether an observed transition is expected <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>, RSI-Anything’s world-model predictions rank actions that a separate policy proposes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cui et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and next-frame feature alignment serves as a training-time regulariser discarded at inference <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>; the recent Agentic-JEPA picks actions by the cosine between predicted next-state and goal embeddings in synthetic text-only environments (100% success in distribution, 0% out of distribution) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rodrigo-Ginés, 2026</a>)</cite>. Decision-aligned work finds that the latent closest to the goal need not be the best action <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026a</a>)</cite> and that predictors can ignore the action <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gan et al., 2026</a>)</cite>; value-equivalent models likewise learn latents for planning without a reconstruction objective <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schrittwieser et al., 2020</a>)</cite>. In GUI-JEPA the JEPA is the policy itself: it scores a11y candidates through candidate-conditioned latents of a frozen GUI-pretrained encoder, with no decoder, whereas earlier GUI work uses a JEPA to describe intent, verify transitions or regularise training. Our mechanism result (<a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 What the latent pathway does ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>) adds a GUI-domain data point to work finding that predictability and action relevance come apart <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and to work that trains world models for the decision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method: GUI-JEPA</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GUI-JEPA chooses each action by scoring candidates. At every step it enumerates the executable actions from the a11y tree, embeds the screenshot once with a frozen JEPA encoder, transforms that screen latent once per candidate with a residual predictor, scores each candidate-conditioned latent and the candidate’s text against the text condition, and executes the highest-scoring candidate (<a href="#S1.F2" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Since no token, pixel or line of code is generated, a decision is one batched forward pass whose cost grows with the number of candidates.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Problem and notation.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We learn a step-level offline policy on AndroidControl <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite> that predicts the recorded action from one step’s inputs and the ground-truth history. A step has a screenshot <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, an a11y tree <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, a text condition <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> (the goal in AC-High, the step instruction in AC-Low) and the ground-truth history <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (the previous action vector and the mean latent change from the previous frame; the text matcher receives the previous actions as text). A frozen encoder gives the screen latent, patch tokens <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}=f_{\theta}(x_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{196\times 1024}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>196</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}=f_{\theta}(x_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{196\times 1024}</annotation></semantics></math>. The candidate set <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}=\mathrm{enumerate}(T_{t})\cup\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>enumerate</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}=\mathrm{enumerate}(T_{t})\cup\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> joins element candidates (a click per enumerated node, an <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> per editable one) with a fixed set <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> of global actions. A candidate <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> carries a 16-d action vector <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> (type one-hot plus coordinates or scroll direction) and, if it has an element, its region <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{roi}(c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>roi</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{roi}(c)</annotation></semantics></math> (global actions: zero region feature, whole-screen pooling). The policy picks <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{c}_{t}=\argmax_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{t}}s(c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>max</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{c}_{t}=\argmax_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{t}}s(c)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Input step and candidates</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Element-level candidates are the visible a11y nodes flagged clickable, long-clickable, editable or scrollable, capped at the 80 smallest by area, which keeps specific elements and bounds the batch; each carries the text of the node and its descendants, its bounding box and its type. Every enumerated node yields a click candidate, and every editable node also an <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> candidate whose text is filled in by the span ranker (<a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Score and select ‣ 3 Method: GUI-JEPA ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>). Global actions act on the whole screen: the four scroll directions, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_back</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_home</span>, <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wait</span> and one <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span>, whose argument is the longest training-vocabulary app name in the text condition. The ground-truth element of a click is the smallest enumerated candidate that contains the recorded click point (details and coverage: <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>JEPA encoder</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is a ViT-L/16 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dosovitskiy et al., 2021</a>, 303M;)</cite>, ImageNet-initialised and pretrained (stage 1) with a JEPA objective adapted from I-JEPA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2023</a>)</cite> on 189K unlabelled mobile (GUI-Odyssey; <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2025</a></cite>) and desktop (VideoCUA; <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jian et al., 2026</a></cite>) screenshots, without action labels or AndroidControl data. The student encoder sees the screenshot <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{x}</annotation></semantics></math> with a random half <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> of its patches zeroed and regresses, at the masked positions, the tokens that an exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{f}</annotation></semantics></math> computes on the full screenshot:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{JEPA}}=\frac{1}{|M|}\sum_{i\in M}\ell_{\mathrm{sL1}}\big(f_{\theta}(\tilde{x})_{i},\ \mathrm{sg}[\bar{f}(x)_{i}]\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>JEPA</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>sL1</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>sg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{JEPA}}=\frac{1}{|M|}\sum_{i\in M}\ell_{\mathrm{sL1}}\big(f_{\theta}(\tilde{x})_{i},\ \mathrm{sg}[\bar{f}(x)_{i}]\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\mathrm{sL1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>sL1</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\mathrm{sL1}}</annotation></semantics></math> the smooth-<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> loss and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{sg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>sg</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{sg}</annotation></semantics></math> the stop-gradient. Random masking suits screenshots, whose content is spread over many small elements, and the latent target spares the encoder from reproducing fonts or colours that do not matter for acting. After two epochs the encoder is frozen and its patch tokens are cached, so policy training never runs the backbone (recipe and hyperparameters: <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>; pretraining–test overlap: <a href="#A7.SS1" title="G.1 Pretraining–test near-duplicates ‣ Appendix G Encoder probe ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Residual latent predictor</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The predictor <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> (39.9M) is a JEPA-style action-conditioned latent predictor that maps the screen latent and one candidate to a candidate-conditioned latent. Its action input concatenates <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> with the ROI-pooled feature <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{c}=\operatorname{pool}_{\operatorname{roi}(c)}(\mathbf{z}_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{1024}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>pool</mi><mrow><mi>roi</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>1024</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{c}=\operatorname{pool}_{\operatorname{roi}(c)}(\mathbf{z}_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{1024}</annotation></semantics></math> of the candidate’s element (zero for global actions), so that two candidates of the same type, such as two buttons, are told apart by what their regions show as well as by their coordinates. An MLP of this pair is added to a learned query token, and a three-layer transformer attends over the 196 patch tokens and the query, giving the candidate-conditioned latent <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}=\mathbf{z}_{t}+\Delta(\mathbf{z}_{t},a_{c},\mathbf{u}_{c})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}=\mathbf{z}_{t}+\Delta(\mathbf{z}_{t},a_{c},\mathbf{u}_{c})</annotation></semantics></math>. The residual form keeps the content of the current screen and lets the predictor express only a candidate-specific change, which preserves the detail needed to ground an element. All candidates of a step form one batch.
<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> is initialised from a dynamics predictor trained on AndroidControl transitions to predict the next step’s latent from <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and the recorded action (<a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>) and is then fine-tuned jointly with the scoring heads. Policy training adds no next-latent loss, and the policy loss alone shapes <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}</annotation></semantics></math> into a decision feature (<a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 What the latent pathway does ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Score and select</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Structural head.</span>
The head pools the candidate-conditioned latent over the candidate’s region (all 196 tokens for global actions) and over the whole screen, and compares an MLP of the pair by cosine with an MLP of the conditioning vector (learned scale <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, per-type bias):</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{split}s_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)={}&amp;\kappa\cos\!\big(\mathrm{MLP}_{v}(\mathbf{v}_{c}),\,\mathrm{MLP}_{t}(\mathrm{cond})\big)\\
&amp;+b_{\mathrm{type}(c)},\end{split}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>lat</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mpadded style="width:1.046em;" width="1.046em"><mi>cos</mi></mpadded><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>MLP</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐯</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="0.507em">,</mo><mi>MLP</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cond</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>type</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{split}s_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)={}&amp;\kappa\cos\!\big(\mathrm{MLP}_{v}(\mathbf{v}_{c}),\,\mathrm{MLP}_{t}(\mathrm{cond})\big)\\
&amp;+b_{\mathrm{type}(c)},\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{c}=[\operatorname{pool}_{\operatorname{roi}(c)}(\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c});\,\mathrm{mean}(\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>pool</mi><mrow><mi>roi</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><mrow><mi>mean</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{c}=[\operatorname{pool}_{\operatorname{roi}(c)}(\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c});\,\mathrm{mean}(\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c})]</annotation></semantics></math>.
<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{cond}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>cond</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{cond}</annotation></semantics></math> joins the frozen CLIP embedding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Radford et al., 2021</a>, 63M;)</cite> of <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. The head’s only candidate-dependent visual input is <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}=\mathbf{z}_{t}+\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}=\mathbf{z}_{t}+\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> reaches it via the residual skip and, independently of the candidate, through <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{cond}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>cond</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{cond}</annotation></semantics></math>. The constraint is deliberate. Everything the head sees of a candidate passes through the predictor, and training cannot bypass the JEPA latent pathway (<a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Design choices and the encoder ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MiniLM text matcher.</span>
The text matcher, a MiniLM-L12 cross-encoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Reimers and Gurevych, 2019</a>, 33M;)</cite>, scores <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> plus the textual action history against the text of each element candidate (<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{text}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>text</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{text}}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for global actions); the two scores are summed outside the structural head, <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s(c)=s_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)+s_{\mathrm{text}}(c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>lat</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>text</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(c)=s_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)+s_{\mathrm{text}}(c)</annotation></semantics></math>. The structural head arbitrates the action type and the eight global actions, which have no text to match, and also contributes at element level, while the text matcher carries most of the grounding among clicks (<a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 What the latent pathway does ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text rankers (stage 3).</span>
Two small rankers refine the arguments without changing which kind of action is taken. The <span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> argument is the top span of the goal-source span ranker, a MiniLM-L6 cross-encoder (22.7M) trained to rank spans of the goal, the text it reads at test time in AC-High (<a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Gains from the two text rankers ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>). If the argmax is a click, the type-gated click reranker <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, a MiniLM-L12 listwise model (33.5M), re-scores the click candidates as <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="s(c)+\beta\,\mathbf{1}[\mathrm{conf}(r)&gt;\tau]\,\tilde{r}(c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold"> 1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>conf</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(c)+\beta\,\mathbf{1}[\mathrm{conf}(r)&gt;\tau]\,\tilde{r}(c)</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}</annotation></semantics></math> its <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-scored logit and <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta,\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta,\tau</annotation></semantics></math> set on validation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Training</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training has three stages (circled numbers in <a href="#S1.F2" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>): JEPA pretraining of the encoder (<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 JEPA encoder ‣ 3 Method: GUI-JEPA ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>), policy training, and the two text rankers. The base policy (predictor, structural head and text matcher, trained jointly; encoder and CLIP text encoder frozen) is trained on the 13,594 cached episodes (74,714 steps) of the 13,604-episode AndroidControl training split with a listwise cross-entropy over the candidates of each step, <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{t}=-w_{t}\log p_{t}(c^{*}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{t}=-w_{t}\log p_{t}(c^{*}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}=\softmax_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{t}}s(c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>softmax</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}=\softmax_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{t}}s(c)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c^{*}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^{*}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the ground-truth candidate and <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{t}{=}1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{t}{=}1.5</annotation></semantics></math> for non-click steps and 1 for clicks, which offsets the predominance of clicks. The objective matches inference, where the recorded action must outscore every alternative the policy could take on that screen. We train with AdamW for 6 epochs, one model for both AC-Low and AC-High (hyperparameters: <a href="#A8.T13" title="In Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>), and fine-tune the predictor jointly, which outperforms freezing it (<a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Design choices and the encoder ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>). The two rankers are then trained on the fixed base policy. Of the 0.50B parameters, 366M are frozen (303M encoder, 63M CLIP text encoder) and <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\approx}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\approx}</annotation></semantics></math>132M trained, including the 22.7M span ranker and the 33.5M click reranker.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmark and splits.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We test on the four official AndroidControl subsplits <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite>: IDD (721 episodes) and the overlapping app_unseen (631), task_unseen (803) and category_unseen (700, contained in task_unseen). The full test set (1,543 episodes, 8,444 steps) and the OOD union (full test minus IDD, 4,586 steps) are the units of evidence. IDD results cover 716 of the 721 episodes (3,858 of 3,897 steps), because five IDD episodes also in OOD subsplits count as OOD (<a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>). The 137-episode validation split selected the click reranker’s variant, weight <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and gate. Systems that state their split report all test subsets together, so we compare them with our full-test result and use IDD only against published IDD numbers.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Protocol.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">AC-Low conditions on the step instruction and AC-High on the episode goal, both with the ground-truth action history. Our exact-match judge keeps the original benchmark’s click rule (the chosen candidate’s centre lies inside the ground-truth element box) and departs from the original protocol in four places: it counts no equivalent <span id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span> or navigation actions, requires the normalised typed text to match, accepts a click for a ground-truth <span id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">long_press</span> (9 IDD steps), and takes the ground-truth box from the smallest enumerated candidate (originally the smallest a11y node), scoring clicks without a candidate (1.6–2.6%) as errors where the original discards them (<a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>). Candidates come from the a11y tree, a privileged input that pixel-only agents do not use.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Main results</h3>

<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S4.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">

<td id="S4.T1.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.2pt;padding-right:3.2pt;">Params</td>

<td id="S4.T1.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.2pt;padding-right:3.2pt;">Judge</td>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Closest published protocol.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The AndroidControl paper’s LoRA-tuned PaLM 2S over a11y text <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>, Tab. 5)</cite> shares our a11y input (we add the screenshot), click rule and subsplits, under the original relaxed judge. In distribution, GUI-JEPA matches it on AC-Low (84.06 vs 83.2) and trails on AC-High (60.99 vs 70.8; <a href="#A3.T6" title="In Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A3.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Exact-match VLM agents.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pixel-only <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">7–8B</span> exact-match entries of <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.2 Main results ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> decode their actions with 14–16<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> more (nominal) parameters than GUI-JEPA. On AC-Low our full-test 78.64 is above OS-Atlas-7B (67.3), MIRAGE-4B (77.6) and Qwen3-VL-8B (77.66), and none of these agents reports a comparable per-step latency.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Examples.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S4.F5" title="In 4.6 Error analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows GUI-JEPA on three real IDD AC-High steps, one per action kind: it picks a menu entry among 15 candidates, opens the app named in the goal, and types a book title copied from the goal, each with one forward pass.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Same-protocol 7B reference</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We also train a same-protocol reference: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> fine-tuned with LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> on 4,000 training episodes for one epoch, one adapter per setting (GUI-JEPA: one model, 13,594 episodes for six; 377-token image), given the same screenshot, candidates and ground-truth history as GUI-JEPA and scored by the same judge on the same 716 IDD episodes. It reaches 91.01 / 70.87 Low / High, and GUI-JEPA reaches 84.06 / 60.99, 92.4% / 86.1% of it, with 6.0% of its parameters (0.498B vs 8.29B; 16.6<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer) and 2.8–4.0<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> its vLLM speed (<a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>). The gap is 7.0 points when the step instruction is given and 9.9 with the goal alone. <a href="#S4.SS6" title="4.6 Error analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.6</span></a> breaks the AC-High gap down by action type.</p>
</div>
</section>

OOD = full test minus IDD; val. = the 137-episode validation split, on which the reranker’s variant, weight and gate were selected.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S4.T2" title="In 4.4 Gains from the two text rankers ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> isolates the two text rankers. Switching the training data of the 22.7M <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> span ranker from step instructions to goal spans adds no parameters and +2.85 IDD High (+2.49 OOD union) by raising IDD High <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> accuracy from 13.5 to 52.5. The type-gated click reranker then adds +1.30 IDD High (+1.33 OOD union) by re-ordering click candidates only. Together they lift OOD-union High from 43.85 to 47.67 and every unseen subsplit by 3.5–4.1 points (<a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>), and the span-ranker gain replicates on the validation split (+2.89 vs +2.85 on IDD).</p>
</div>
</section>
