<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span><span id="S4.T3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Same-hardware latency per real step</span> (ms; peak GPU memory in GB; same 100 AC-High IDD steps, one H20, batch 1). 7B = Qwen2.5-VL-7B (zero-shot and unmerged-LoRA timings: <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>); <math id="S4.T3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math>: vLLM pre-allocates at least the weights. <math id="S4.T3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> ours: the 7B agent’s p50 divided by our fp32 or bf16 p50.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.36877v1/fig_timebudget.svg" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/244;" width="476" height="244"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span><span id="S4.F3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Where a step’s time goes</span> (segment means, 100 shared real steps, one H20, batch 1; medians: <a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Decoding takes half or more of the 7B step, and its prefill alone outlasts a whole GUI-JEPA step.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.36877v1/fig_mechanism.png" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/129;" width="476" height="129" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span><span id="S4.F4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The scorer relies on the latent pathway, which needs no dynamics pretraining.</span> (a) Evaluation-time lesions (IDD; OOD and retrained controls in <a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> and <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). (b) Pilot AC-Low (an early configuration without the text matcher): only the structural head uses the pathway (orange box: deployed design). (c) Change in IDD accuracy against the jointly fine-tuned, dynamics-pretrained predictor when the predictor is kept frozen or randomly initialised (identical recipe).</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">What the comparison fixes.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The timing compares a scored step with a decoded step at fixed inputs, hardware and batch size. Both systems receive the same 100 real AC-High IDD screenshots, candidates and histories on one H20 at batch 1, and differ in model, training data and computation (<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Same-protocol 7B reference ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>). GUI-JEPA’s timing starts at JPEG decoding and covers CPU candidate and ROI preparation; the 7B agent’s starts at image preprocessing and tokenisation. Screenshot capture, a11y retrieval and GUI-JEPA’s once-per-episode CLIP goal embedding (5.6 ms) are excluded.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Speed.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The final GUI-JEPA pipeline (base policy, span ranker and click reranker) needs a median 74 ms per step in fp32 and 51.5 ms with bf16 autocast, against 207 ms for the 7B agent with vLLM and 507 ms with HF transformers (merged LoRA; <a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). GUI-JEPA is thus 2.8<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> (fp32) to 4.0<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> (bf16) faster than vLLM and 6.8–9.8<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than HF, with 4.6–6.4<math id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> less peak GPU memory. In bf16 it makes the same predictions as in fp32 on all 200 timed steps, including the typed text (<a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Where the time goes.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> splits the mean step time on the same 100 steps. Decoding takes 51% (vLLM) to 60% (HF) of the 7B agent’s step, on top of its prefill, and the vLLM prefill alone outlasts a whole fp32 GUI-JEPA step, so the gain comes from both the smaller model and the absence of decoding. About half of a GUI-JEPA step goes to the batched predictor and head, which bf16 speeds up threefold, and its cost grows with the number of candidates (<a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>Error analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Clicks, 63% of the steps, account for 5.8 of the 9.9-point AC-High gap to the 7B agent, shared between choosing the click type and grounding the element, the part the text matcher carries (<a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Score and select ‣ 3 Method: GUI-JEPA ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>). On global actions the gap lies mainly in the type decision, and on <span id="S4.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span> and <span id="S4.SS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> in the argument (per type: <a href="#A8.T15" title="In Same-protocol 7B reference. ‣ Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>). The two systems also err on different steps (<a href="#A9.F10" title="In Where the GUI-JEPA step time goes. ‣ Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>): at least one of them is right on 78.7% of IDD AC-High steps, and the margin between GUI-JEPA’s top two scores flags its errors (AUROC 0.74), so uncertain steps can be routed to a same-protocol 7B agent where accuracy matters more than speed (<a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Confidence routing to the 7B agent ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.36877v1/fig_qual_jepa.png" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/93;" width="476" height="93" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span><span id="S4.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GUI-JEPA on three real AC-High IDD steps</span>, one per action kind: (a) an element click, (b) a global action, (c) a typed argument that the span ranker copies from the goal. Each step takes one scoring pass over all its candidates (<math id="S4.F5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>: probability of the chosen action; boxes: ground truth in green, GUI-JEPA’s choice in purple).</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Analysis</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>What the latent pathway does</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reliance.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We lesion the trained base policy at evaluation time, text matcher untouched (<a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>a; <a href="#A2.T5" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). On IDD, shuffling the action vectors across all candidates costs 27.2 Low / 23.4 High, shuffling them within a type 11.2 / 10.8 (mostly scroll directions; about 5 High on clicks), and replacing the candidate-conditioned latent by the current latent (no predictor) 24.9 / 14.0, mostly on the global actions, which share the full-screen ROI. The action vector reaches the structural head only through the predictor, and training cannot route around it. Retrained at full scale with the identity map in place of the predictor, the policy reaches 62.36 / 42.33, 21.4 / 14.5 points below the base policy, again on the global actions, which the identity map leaves indistinguishable (<a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). The pathway thus carries chiefly action type and scroll direction, and also helps select among clicks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The pathway is trained for the decision.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A randomly initialised predictor trained with the identical full-scale recipe does as well as the dynamics-pretrained one (+0.50 High / <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.01</annotation></semantics></math> Low; <a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>c), and predictive auxiliary objectives (per-patch <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, pooled, multi-horizon, LeWorldModel-style <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maes et al., 2026</a>)</cite>) add nothing at 4K-episode scale (<a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). The predictor thus learns what the decision needs, and forward-model probes show that it forecasts the next latent worse than a copy of the current one (<a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>). It acts as an action- and ROI-conditioned transform of the current screen, so a JEPA policy for GUIs needs no dynamics pretraining. This agrees with findings that predictability and action relevance come apart <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and with training world models for the decision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Design choices and the encoder</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At pilot scale without the text matcher, the residual form raises AC-Low from 40.6 to 43.9, whereas a predictor that re-synthesises the whole latent lowers AC-Low click grounding to 34.8, below the identity map’s 46.8. The structural head makes the policy use the predictor. Replacing the predictor by the identity map costs it 8.9 AC-Low points (40.6 vs 31.7), whereas a concat-MLP head that also sees raw candidate features stays within 1.4 points with or without a predictor (<a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>b). Conditioning on the previous action and frame change adds 8 High points; at full scale, joint fine-tuning beats a frozen predictor by 3.8 AC-Low / 1.9 AC-High IDD points (<a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>c; alternatives: <a href="#A5.T10" title="In Appendix E Design alternatives not adopted ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>). The encoder is cheap to obtain. After 0.76 GPU-hours of JEPA pretraining on unlabelled screenshots, its frozen tokens score 67.22 on a coarse localisation probe over ScreenSpot-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite> (probe hit@8; random-init ViT-L: 58.8), on par with DINOv3-ViT-L <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Siméoni et al., 2026</a>)</cite> (65.28; <a href="#A7.F7" title="In Appendix G Encoder probe ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Encoder probe ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>). In the policy, DINOv2-L <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2024</a>)</cite> features at 518 px instead cost 17.4 / 9.8 points at 4K-episode scale, though it also changes the input resolution (<a href="#A5.T10" title="In Appendix E Design alternatives not adopted ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first GUI agent whose policy is built on a JEPA, replaces action decoding with one batched scoring pass over candidate-conditioned JEPA latents. With 0.50B parameters it needs 51.5–74 ms per step, <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">2.8–4.0<math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math></span> less than a vLLM-served 7B agent on the same inputs, and reaches 92.4% / 86.1% of its IDD Low / High accuracy with 6.0% of its parameters.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The JEPA latent pathway is essential to the scorer (lesions cost 10.8–23.4 IDD High points) and is trained for the decision: a randomly initialised predictor does as well as a dynamics-pretrained one. A JEPA used as a GUI action scorer should thus be judged by the decisions it supports, not by next-latent fidelity, and can be trained for them directly. Extending such scorers from steps to tasks is the next step for JEPA-based GUI agents.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GUI-JEPA consumes the a11y tree, a privileged structured input that pixel-only agents do not use; the 1.6–2.6% of test clicks without a candidate count as errors, and every latency excludes screen capture and a11y retrieval. The policy is a step-level scorer; online task completion, which needs a termination head and a planner, is left to future work, as is using the predictor as a forward model. Design choices other than the reranker’s variant, weight and gate were made on test IDD and re-checked on validation only for the span ranker and overall base-policy accuracy (<a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Gains from the two text rankers ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>). Speed-ups are measured at batch 1 against vLLM and HF serving of the 7B agent (<a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>). The same-protocol 7B reference is one LoRA adapter per setting trained on 4,000 of 13,594 episodes. The method is specialised to mobile a11y candidates; other candidate sources, such as web DOM nodes, need their own candidate texts and action vectors. Non-JEPA encoders are compared through a probe on the frozen tokens (<a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Encoder probe ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>); a comparison inside the full-scale policy is future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Ethical Considerations</h2>

<div id="Sx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GUI-JEPA lowers the cost of GUI agents that act on a user’s device. A wrong action, such as sending a message, deleting data or confirming a payment, can be hard to undo, and step-level errors remain common; a deployment needs user confirmation before irreversible actions. The speed that makes on-device agents practical also makes it cheaper to automate interactions meant for humans, such as mass account creation. The policy reads the accessibility tree, which can contain personal on-screen data; running the 0.50B model on-device keeps that data local. We use only public datasets under their licences (AndroidControl Apache-2.0, GUI-Odyssey CC-BY-4.0, VideoCUA and ScreenSpot-Pro MIT), collect no new data, and involve no human subjects, annotators or crowd workers.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Reproducibility statement</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The encoder is a ViT-L/16 at 224 px, initialised from ImageNet weights and trained with a JEPA objective adapted from I-JEPA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2023</a>)</cite> on 189,262 unlabelled screenshots from GUI-Odyssey <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and VideoCUA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jian et al., 2026</a>)</cite> for 2 epochs (<math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx</annotation></semantics></math>0.76 GPU-hour on one H20), with no action labels and no AndroidControl data (<a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 JEPA encoder ‣ 3 Method: GUI-JEPA ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sections</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> and <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>). The policy is trained on the 13,594 cached episodes of the 13,604-episode AndroidControl training split <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite> with a listwise cross-entropy, AdamW and 6 epochs, for three seeds (<a href="#S3.SS5" title="3.5 Training ‣ 3 Method: GUI-JEPA ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sections</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a> and <a href="#A8.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>). We evaluate on the official test subsplits with the exact-match judge of <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> and time both systems on the same 100 real IDD steps on one H20 at batch 1 (<a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Protocol details</h2>

<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Splits and overlap.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The official <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">test_subsplits.json</span> of AndroidControl <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite> lists 721 IDD, 631 app_unseen, 803 task_unseen and 700 category_unseen episodes, whose union is the full test set of 1,543 episodes and 8,444 steps. The subsplits are not disjoint: every category_unseen episode is also a task_unseen episode, and app_unseen shares 606 episodes with category_unseen and 607 with task_unseen. We therefore treat the full test set and the OOD union (full test minus IDD as evaluated: 827 episodes, 4,586 steps) as the units of evidence and report the three OOD subsplits, each evaluated in full, only as a breakdown (<a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>). Five of the 721 IDD episodes also appear in OOD subsplits and count as OOD, so every IDD accuracy in the paper is computed on 716 episodes and 3,858 of the 3,897 steps (99.0%); the coverage analysis below uses all 721 episodes. The 137-episode validation split (690 steps) selected the click reranker’s variant, its weight <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and its confidence gate. Every other design choice, including both text rankers, was made on test IDD; the validation row of <a href="#A3.T6" title="In Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> checks how these choices carry over. We train on 13,594 of the 13,604 training episodes of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2024, Tab. 3)</a></cite> (74,714 of 74,722 steps).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Candidate enumeration and coverage.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Element-level candidates are the visible accessibility-tree (a11y) nodes flagged clickable, long-clickable, editable or scrollable, plus containers that inherit clickability, de-duplicated by bounds and capped at the 80 smallest by area; editable nodes also yield <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> candidates. Global actions are the four scroll directions, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_back</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_home</span>, <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wait</span> and one <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span>, whose argument is the longest training-vocabulary app name in the goal or instruction. A ground-truth click or long-press is mapped to the smallest enumerated candidate that contains its coordinate, whereas the original benchmark takes the smallest a11y node of any kind; the click rule itself (the chosen candidate’s centre inside the ground-truth box) is unchanged. When no candidate contains the coordinate the step is unmapped and counts as an error for our policy (the original benchmark discards such steps). The mapped fraction is 97.4–98.4% on the test subsplits (IDD 98.0%, 2,405 of 2,454 click and long-press steps; full test 97.6%, 4,961 of 5,083), 98.8% on validation and 98.4% on the training split. An IDD step has 23.6 a11y candidates on average (median 18, p95 57; 22.2 on the full test set and 23.2 on the training split), and the 80-candidate cap is reached on 16 IDD, 22 full-test and 272 training steps. Per-type IDD step counts are in <a href="#A8.T15" title="In Same-protocol 7B reference. ‣ Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Judge.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A step is correct under our exact-match judge when the predicted action type equals the ground-truth type and the argument matches: a click when the centre of the chosen candidate lies inside the ground-truth element box, which is the click rule of the original benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>, App. D.3)</cite>; an <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> when the typed string equals the ground-truth string after normalisation; <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span> and scroll when the argument matches exactly. The judge departs from the original protocol in four places, in both directions. (i) It is stricter in accepting no equivalent actions, whereas the original protocol treats <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span> and a click on an element bearing the app name as equivalent, and likewise <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_back</span> and a click on the on-screen Back button. (ii) It is more lenient on <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span>: it compares the normalised text only, whereas the original protocol scores typing as an element action that also requires the target element to lie inside the ground-truth box and the text to be identical. (iii) It is more lenient in accepting a click for a ground-truth <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">long_press</span> (9 IDD steps). (iv) It takes the ground-truth box from our enumerated candidates: a mapped click is judged against a box at least as large as the original’s smallest a11y node (more lenient), while an unmapped click counts as an error, where <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2024, App. D.1)</a></cite> discard it (stricter). On click steps, 62.7% of IDD steps, both judges thus apply the same centre-in-box rule. Exact-match (EM) re-evaluations in the literature are the closest published protocol; numbers under the original relaxed protocol are not interchangeable with ours.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conditioning and seeds.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One trained model serves both settings: AC-Low conditions on the step instruction and AC-High on the episode goal; both receive the ground-truth action history. We train three policy seeds. The main text reports seed 3, the best seed on every test split, at every stage and in both settings; full-scale results in this appendix are means <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> sd over the three seeds unless a seed is named, and <a href="#A2.T4" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> list every seed. For <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}3</annotation></semantics></math> the 95% <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-interval half-width, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.30\,\mathrm{sd}/\sqrt{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>4.30</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>sd</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.30\,\mathrm{sd}/\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, is about <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>2.4 points (IDD High <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>2.37, full-test High <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>2.34, IDD Low <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>2.52). Seeds capture training variance only, so external comparisons also use episode-clustered bootstrap intervals (<a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Episode-clustered bootstrap intervals ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span><span id="A2.T4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Per-seed step accuracy of the three policy seeds</span> at every stage of the waterfall (exact match; bold: seed 3, reported in the main text). Stages share the base checkpoint of each seed; the span ranker is trained once and shared by the three seeds, the click reranker once per seed. The OOD union is derived per seed from the full-test and IDD step counts.</figcaption>

<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Episode-clustered bootstrap intervals</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because steps of one episode are correlated, the bootstrap for the external comparisons (<a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.2 Main results ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) resamples test episodes. Each of <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B{=}2{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B{=}2{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> resamples draws the 716 IDD (or 1,543 full-test) episodes with replacement and keeps every step of a drawn episode; the same resample is applied to the per-step predictions of the three seeds of the final system, whose step accuracies are averaged, and the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of this seed-averaged accuracy form the 95% interval (the per-step predictions reproduce the reported accuracies exactly). The intervals are 60.12 [58.45, 61.85] High and 83.09 [81.72, 84.41] Low on IDD, and 52.85 [51.59, 54.04] High and 77.63 [76.62, 78.63] Low on the full test set (77.64 in <a href="#A2.T4" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> averages per-seed results rounded to two decimals). For seed 3 alone they are 60.99 [58.95, 62.97] High and 84.06 [82.46, 85.47] Low on IDD, and 53.75 [52.40, 55.06] High and 78.64 [77.61, 79.70] Low on the full test set. The bootstrap covers test-episode sampling and the <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-interval over seeds covers training variance; neither covers the protocol differences listed in <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.2 Main results ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span><span id="A3.T6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Per-subsplit waterfall on AC-High, with the a11y-text PaLM 2S cells (closest published protocol).</span> Exact-match step accuracy of the base policy, after the goal-source span ranker and after the type-gated click reranker (final system); mean <math id="A3.T6.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> sd over 3 training seeds on identical base checkpoints (per seed: <a href="#A2.T4" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). <math id="A3.T6.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is final minus base; <math id="A3.T6.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> and all differences in the text use unrounded means. The OOD union is derived per seed from the full-test and IDD results; the validation split selected the reranker’s variant, <math id="A3.T6.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and gate. PaLM 2S: the LoRA-tuned a11y-text model of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2024, Tab. 5)</a></cite> on the same subsplits under the original protocol. The OOD subsplits overlap (<a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>). AC-Low: <a href="#A3.T7" title="In Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>

The PaLM 2S AC-Low setting also receives the episode goal.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.36877v1/fig_waterfall.svg" id="A3.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/174;" width="476" height="174"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span><span id="A3.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The text rankers’ gains transfer across subsplits.</span> AC-High step accuracy (3 training seeds, mean <math id="A3.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> sd) of the base policy, after the span ranker and after the click reranker, on IDD, the three overlapping OOD subsplits and the full test set; increments are computed on identical base checkpoints. Numbers: <a href="#A3.T6" title="In Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A3.T6" title="In Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A3.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and <a href="#A3.F6" title="In Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> break the waterfall of <a href="#S4.T2" title="In 4.4 Gains from the two text rankers ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> down by subsplit. The AC-High gains transfer: on the three OOD subsplits the span ranker adds 2.08–2.76 points, and the click reranker adds 1.04–1.17 on the full test set, the OOD union and every OOD subsplit, at least its 0.98 on IDD. Neither stage changes the action-type decision of the base policy, but AC-Low pays a small cost. The single span ranker, trained on goals, also supplies the typed argument for AC-Low step instructions and lowers AC-Low on every seed (by 1.18 points on the OOD union): on the full test set it raises High <span id="A3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> accuracy from 17.7 to 53.7 (IDD: 12.3 to 53.4) but lowers Low <span id="A3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> accuracy from 83.4 to 74.4. The click reranker, which raises IDD High click grounding given the type from 71.8 to 73.7, also runs in AC-Low and recovers 0.53 of the 1.18 OOD-union points, leaving OOD-union AC-Low 0.65 below the base policy.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On the validation split the waterfall keeps the test ordering and step sizes (+3.04 and +0.87 High). The span-ranker step is thus a held-out replication of a choice made on test IDD. The reranker step is not, because the reranker’s variant, <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and gate were selected on this split; its held-out evidence is the test-set gain.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The PaLM 2S columns give the only published baseline that consumes the a11y tree (text only, no screenshot) with our click rule and subsplits; its AC-Low setting receives the episode goal together with the step instruction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, while ours receives the step instruction only. Averaged over the three seeds, GUI-JEPA matches it on IDD AC-Low (83.09 vs 83.2) and trails by 10.7 AC-High points; out of distribution it trails by 12.2–13.9 High and 4.2–6.1 Low points.</p>
</div>
</section>

Top: inference-time lesions on all steps of each split, text matcher untouched except in the last row; the as-is row is an independent evaluation of the same policies (on IDD within 0.2 of <a href="#A2.T4" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Middle: training-time variants (base-policy OOD: the as-is row); the two retrained rows use the identical full-scale recipe (OOD on all steps); the parameter-matched row lists its three training runs on IDD, and <sup id="A4.T8.6" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A4.T8.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">§</span></sup>marks the mean of the two that train stably (the third collapses on clicks: 45.5–47.7 Low / 28.8–31.4 High out of distribution). Bottom: predictive objectives at 4K-episode scale (auxiliary losses with <math id="A4.T8.m56" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda{=}0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda{=}0.1</annotation></semantics></math>; multi-horizon InfoNCE 0.2), AC-High change against the matched 4K reference, paired per seed unless a mean is stated. <div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> collects the evidence on the latent-predictor pathway summarised in <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 What the latent pathway does ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>; the text below adds only what the table does not show.</p>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inference-time lesions.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The lesions are applied at evaluation time to the trained full-scale base policies (text rankers off), so they measure how much the trained scorer relies on the pathway; the retrained controls below test whether it is needed. Removing the predictor (<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}:=\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c}:=\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>) hurts mainly the global actions: of its 21.9 AC-Low / 14.6 AC-High IDD points, 19.0 / 14.1 fall on scroll, <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span> and <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_back</span> (19.6 / 15.6 with <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wait</span>). These share the full-screen ROI, so without the predictor their action vectors no longer reach the score and the three types are never chosen correctly, while click accuracy barely moves (83.9 to 83.2 Low, 58.4 to 60.6 High). The within-type shuffle, which permutes the four scroll directions, costs 8.6 / 6.3 points on scroll steps and 2.3 / 4.2 on clicks. Without the text matcher the structural head’s click grounding is 30.9 Low / 31.8 High against 89.8 / 71.8 for the full scorer: the matcher carries most of the click grounding, while the head alone still grounds about a third of the click steps whose type it gets right. The reliance holds on every OOD subsplit; for the main-text model, removing the predictor costs 21.7–23.1 Low / 7.9–9.7 High points there, the within-type shuffle 10.5–11.5 / 8.5–9.0 and the all-candidate shuffle 24.4–25.0 / 15.4–16.7 (means: <a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training-time variants.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Freezing the dynamics-pretrained predictor costs 2.52 AC-Low / 1.25 AC-High IDD points on average (3.78 / 1.89 for seed 3; <a href="#A2.T5" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). A randomly initialised predictor trained jointly with the identical full-scale recipe matches the dynamics-pretrained one: its High is higher for every seed (+0.50 to +1.17) and its Low within 1.01 points. At pilot scale, the identity map gives 31.73 Low vs 40.59 for the ROI-conditioned predictor (structural head, no text matcher; <a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>b), and training on shuffled dynamics with a frozen predictor gives 47.33 / 28.46 vs 62.70 / 38.96.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Retrained controls.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrained from scratch at full scale with the identical recipe, the identity map in place of the predictor again never chooses scroll, <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span> or <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_back</span> correctly (<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-11.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>11.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-11.3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-5.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-5.1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-2.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2.6</annotation></semantics></math> Low points), while clicks change by <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.8</annotation></semantics></math> Low / <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.2</annotation></semantics></math> High points. The matcher-only policy scores 0–12% on scroll, <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">open_app</span>, <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_back</span>, <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wait</span> and <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span>, and its click grounding is 88.4 / 68.2 against the base policy’s 89.8 / 71.8. A no-predictor control tests whether the predictor is needed at all once the action reaches the score: its structural head receives <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\operatorname{pool}_{\operatorname{roi}(c)}(\mathbf{z}_{t});\,\mathrm{mean}(\mathbf{z}_{t});\,a_{c}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>pool</mi><mrow><mi>roi</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><mrow><mi>mean</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\operatorname{pool}_{\operatorname{roi}(c)}(\mathbf{z}_{t});\,\mathrm{mean}(\mathbf{z}_{t});\,a_{c}]</annotation></semantics></math> through an MLP matched in parameters to the predictor and the original projection (41.09M against 39.91M + 1.18M), with matcher, history, type bias and recipe unchanged. It matches the base policy in two of three seeds (<a href="#A2.T5" title="In B.1 Per-seed results ‣ Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>; within 1.4 points on app- and category-unseen) and collapses on clicks in the third (click grounding 48.3 Low against 89.6 for its base seed). Given the action vector directly, a parameter-matched head on the same JEPA latents thus reaches the base policy’s accuracy when its training succeeds, whereas the predictor trains stably in all three seeds; either way the action is scored on the JEPA latent, consistent with the predictor’s role as an action- and ROI-conditioned transform of it (<a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 What the latent pathway does ‣ 5 Analysis ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The bottom block of <a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> gives the predictive auxiliary objectives as AC-High changes against the matched 4K reference; none improves on it (<a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Design alternatives not adopted ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Forward-model probes.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A4.T9" title="In Predictive objectives. ‣ Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows that the deployed predictor is a poor forward model: its output is further from the true next latent than a copy of the current latent, and its predicted change has near-zero cosine to the true change and points the right way at chance rate. Feeding a shuffled action leaves the predicted latent at cosine 0.86 to the true-action prediction (IDD). The randomly initialised predictor of <a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> (150 IDD episodes, 782 steps) is no more action-sensitive: its predicted change has cosine 0.002 to the true change, its ground-truth AUC equals the deployed predictor’s (0.5426 vs 0.5425; chance 0.5), and a shuffled action leaves its output at cosine 0.887 (0.954 for a within-type shuffle, probed for this predictor only). Free-running <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-step rollouts of the dynamics-pretrained predictor that initialises the deployed one (400 episodes; 1,500 / 1,500 / 1,349 queries at <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> / 2 / 3), scored by cosine to the true latent <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> steps ahead, never beat persistence (keeping <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>): 0.745 against 0.793 at <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> (0.733 with shuffled actions), 0.510 against 0.749 at <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}2</annotation></semantics></math> and 0.322 against 0.741 at <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}3</annotation></semantics></math>. The rollout beats persistence on 39 / 10 / 2% of steps and a shuffled-action rollout on only 43 / 48 / 49%; only within-episode retrieval of the true frame at <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> slightly favours it (R@5 79.7 vs 77.2 for persistence). Its one-step cosine (0.745) exceeds the deployed predictor’s 0.467, consistent with joint fine-tuning on the policy loss moving the predictor away from next-latent prediction; both are below copying (0.793 / 0.788).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scoring head.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The concat-MLP head trades AC-Low for AC-High accuracy: against the structural head it loses AC-Low and gains AC-High points with the ROI-conditioned predictor, and likewise loses 7.3 Low and gains 8.8 High with an <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>-conditioned predictor (40.51 / 18.43 vs 33.18 / 27.19). Its AC-Low accuracy is the same with either predictor or none (<a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>b), so whatever it gains does not come through the predictor, whereas the structural head drops from 40.59 to 31.73 when the predictor is replaced by the identity map. We keep the structural head because it forces the policy through the candidate-conditioned latent; the higher pilot-scale High of the concat head shows that this constraint has a cost at that scale. Conditioning the structural head on the previous action and frame change (implicit action history) was adopted: it gains 8.0 High at pilot scale without the text matcher (23.35 to 31.39, at a cost of 4.4 Low) and 7.1 High with it (31.91 to 38.96, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.6</annotation></semantics></math> Low), and the final system uses it together with the textual action history in the matcher query.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Encoder and resolution.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Swapping in DINOv2-L features <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2024</a>)</cite> changes the encoder and the resolution (518 px) together, so this comparison does not isolate the effect of resolution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Predictor objectives.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Predictive auxiliary losses on the predictor do not help (<a href="#A4.T8" title="In Appendix D Mechanism analyses ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, bottom). The leakage-free pooled next-latent MSE has a low mean because one of its three runs collapses; the other two are within 1.3 points of their paired controls. Our SIGReg-style regulariser simplifies SIGReg <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Balestriero and
LeCun, 2025</a>)</cite>: where LeJEPA uses the Epps–Pulley statistic, it penalises the mean and variance of 256 random projections of the pooled predicted latents, and it acts on frozen encoder features, whereas LeWorldModel <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maes et al., 2026</a>)</cite> trains end to end.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

Every cell is copied from the cited table. Apart from LiMAC and its two baselines, discussed in the text, none is set against our numbers because input, judge or split differ (ours for reference: 77.64 / 52.85 Low / High on the full test and 83.09 / 60.12 on IDD as 3-seed means, 78.64 / 53.75 and 84.06 / 60.99 for seed 3, under the exact-match judge with a11y input). Judge: <em id="A6.T11.15" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">relaxed</em> = original protocol; <em id="A6.T11.16" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">OS-Atlas</em> = a click within 14% of the screen width counts and typed text at F1<math id="A6.T11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>0.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025</a>, App. D)</cite>; <em id="A6.T11.17" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">own</em> = the paper’s own definition. Split: <em id="A6.T11.18" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">7,708</em> = OS-Atlas test samples; <em id="A6.T11.19" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">r500</em> / <em id="A6.T11.20" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">r800</em> = a random 500- / 800-step test subset; <em id="A6.T11.21" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">r500-IDD</em> = IDD part of Random-500; <em id="A6.T11.22" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unspec.</em> = not stated in the source; <em id="A6.T11.23" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">AC-v2 (398)</em> = the 398-example cleaned subset of GUI-Libra (its Pass@1 columns). <sup id="A6.T11.24" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T11.24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup>Goal-conditioned per-step action accuracy (“overall accuracy”), the analogue of AC-High. Parameter counts are nominal.</figcaption>
