<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12: </span><span id="A6.T12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Zero-shot and larger models under other protocols, or with AC-High only</span> (conventions and judge / split definitions as in <a href="#A6.T11" title="In Appendix F Other-protocol baselines ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>). Every cell is copied from the cited table; none is set against our numbers. MAI-UI reports exact match on an unstated split and no AC-Low.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.T11" title="In Appendix F Other-protocol baselines ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> and <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ Appendix F Other-protocol baselines ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> list the AndroidControl results of small models and of larger or zero-shot systems reported under protocols that <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.2 Main results ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> does not include; their judge, split and input columns show why none except LiMAC is set against our numbers. None of the larger models is evaluated on the full test set we use.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">LiMAC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christianos et al., 2025</a>)</cite> is the closest small agent that also consumes the UI tree: an action transformer (AcT, <math id="A6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx</annotation></semantics></math>520M) over UI-element embeddings combined with Florence-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> (820M as deployed by LiMAC), which receives the screenshot annotated with numbered element boxes and the goal. Its overall accuracy is a goal-conditioned per-step action accuracy, the analogue of our AC-High setting, under its own judge (a predicted element whose box lies within the target element is correct, typed text is accepted at a Jaccard index of at least 0.5) on “the test set”, with no sub-split or size given; its confusion matrix sums to 3,708 steps, matching none of the official sub-splits. LiMAC and Florence-2 alone are 10.3 and 4.2 points above our 3-seed mean full-test High (9.3 and 3.2 above seed 3) with 2.7<math id="A6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> and 1.6<math id="A6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> our parameters, and its fine-tuned Qwen2-VL-2B baseline is 0.65 below our mean with 4.0<math id="A6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> our parameters; LiMAC’s more lenient text rule and unstated split keep the comparison approximate. LiMAC reports 0.34 s per step (Florence-2 alone: 0.50 s) on unspecified hardware, against our 51.5–74 ms per real step on one H20 (<a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">With the three-seed mean full-test AC-Low (77.64; seed 3: 78.64), GUI-JEPA is level with Qwen3-VL-8B (77.7) and MIRAGE-4B (77.6) of <a href="#S4.T1" title="In 4.2 Main results ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Encoder probe</h2>

<figure id="A7.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.36877v1/fig_encoder.svg" id="A7.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/166;" width="476" height="166"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span><span id="A7.F7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lenient frozen-encoder localisation probe across pretraining recipes.</span> ScreenSpot-Pro hit@8 of a soft-argmax localisation probe on frozen patch tokens (our encoders: mean <math id="A7.F7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> sd over 5 probe seeds); hit@8 accepts errors up to 57% of the image side. Points, left to right: a web anchor (<math id="A7.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx</annotation></semantics></math>77K web screenshots, 60 epochs); mobile-only (119K GUI-Odyssey screenshots, 2 epochs); desktop-only (70K VideoCUA screenshots, 2 epochs); the policy encoder (blue; the mixed 189K mobile and desktop recipe, 2 epochs); a replicate pretraining of the same recipe after 2 epochs and, continued, after 4 and 6 epochs; DINOv3-ViT-L with its 95% bootstrap interval over probe examples (band). The recipes also differ in data size and training length, and the probe measures coarse localisation only (see text).</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Probe.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A7.F7" title="In Appendix G Encoder probe ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> compares pretraining recipes for the frozen encoder by a localisation probe on its patch tokens: a linear scorer per patch, a softmax over the <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14\times 14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14\times 14</annotation></semantics></math> grid and a soft-argmax give a point that is regressed (MSE) onto the centre of the target box; the encoder is fixed and only the probe is trained. hit@<math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is the fraction of held-out examples whose predicted point lies within <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k/14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k/14</annotation></semantics></math> of the image side (normalised Euclidean distance) of the target centre, so hit@8 accepts errors of up to 128 px on the 224-px input. The probe is lenient: on the 1,581 held-out ScreenSpot-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite> examples the policy encoder’s hit@8 of 67.22 <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> 0.91 comes with a hit@3 of 10.36 <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> 0.36, a hit@1 of 0.92 <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> 0.36 and a mean error of 0.509 of the image side (114 px); on 255 ScreenSpot-v2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> examples it reaches 90.59 <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> 1.00 hit@8 with a mean error of 0.378 of the side (85 px). For calibration, under the same probe a randomly initialised ViT-L reaches 87.8 hit@8 on the same ScreenSpot-v2 split and 58.8 [56.4, 61.2] on ScreenSpot-Pro, and an ImageNet-initialised ViT-L without GUI pretraining 58.1. The probe thus measures coarse localisation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Recipes.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under this probe the mixed recipe, I-JEPA-style pretraining <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2023</a>)</cite> of an ImageNet-initialised ViT-L on 119K GUI-Odyssey <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> mobile and 70K VideoCUA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jian et al., 2026</a>)</cite> desktop frames for 2 epochs, scores at least as high as every other recipe in <a href="#A7.F7" title="In Appendix G Encoder probe ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>: either domain alone, a web anchor trained for 60 epochs on the 76,838 viewport and full-page screenshots of the class-balanced 7K split (Web-7k-Resampled) of WebUI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, and DINOv3-ViT-L <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Siméoni et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, trained on 1.7B images. DINOv3’s 95% bootstrap interval over probe examples, [62.9, 67.6], contains the policy encoder’s 67.22 (95% <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-interval over probe seeds [66.1, 68.3]): under this probe the policy encoder is at DINOv3’s level, and since the two intervals cover different sources of variance (probe seeds against probe examples), they do not order the encoders. The replicate uses the same data, batch size and learning-rate schedule and continues to 6 epochs: after 2 epochs (JEPA loss 0.668 against 0.677 for the policy encoder) it gives 67.82, and its 4- and 6-epoch scores show that training longer does not help. The 0.6-point gap between the two 2-epoch encoders is a rough measure of pretraining variance, which the per-recipe sds, computed over probe seeds, do not capture. The recipes also differ in data size (189K / 119K / 70K / <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx</annotation></semantics></math>77K screenshots) and training length (2 to 60 epochs), so the comparison does not identify which ingredient matters. Two further recipes do not lift the probe mean: initialising JEPA pretraining from DINOv3 lowers it, and action-conditioned pretraining in the style of V-JEPA 2-AC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2025</a>)</cite> on VideoCUA stays at the level of the web anchor.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The probe measures frozen localisation features: the recipe is a 0.76 GPU-hour route to frozen GUI features that localise as well as the alternatives. In the policy, the 4K-scale swap to DINOv2-L at 518 px (<a href="#A5.T10" title="In Appendix E Design alternatives not adopted ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>) changes the encoder and the resolution together.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Pretraining–test near-duplicates</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We hashed the 9,987 screenshots of the 1,543 AndroidControl test episodes (pHash and dHash, 64 bits) against the 189,262 pretraining screenshots (118,791 GUI-Odyssey, 70,471 VideoCUA). 58 test frames (0.58%) in 43 episodes have a verified near-duplicate (pHash distance <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 8</annotation></semantics></math> and normalised cross-correlation <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 0.9</annotation></semantics></math>), all from GUI-Odyssey and showing generic system screens. For calibration, the same pHash threshold matches 35.0% of test frames to the frames of 4,000 AndroidControl training episodes (different episodes of the same benchmark) and 9.5% to the pretraining set; random pairs have a median distance of 32. Removing the 43 episodes changes final High and Low by <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.2</annotation></semantics></math> (High 59.90 vs 60.12 on IDD, 52.64 vs 52.85 on the full test). Removing every episode with any pHash match within distance 8 (549 episodes), a criterion that also flags generic layouts, gives 58.74 IDD and 51.14 full-test High. At the app level, 29 app names match exactly and 26% of test episodes touch a package that also appears in GUI-Odyssey, with different devices and tasks and no shared screenshots. Pretraining–test leakage is thus negligible for the reported numbers.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<span id="A8.T13.2.12.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">MiniLM-L12 listwise reranker over the click candidates; <math id="A8.T13.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{final}=\mathrm{base}+\beta\,\tilde{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>final</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>base</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{final}=\mathrm{base}+\beta\,\tilde{r}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A8.T13.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A8.T13.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-scored reranker logit, applied only when the base argmax is a click and the reranker confidence exceeds the gate, in both settings; variant, <math id="A8.T13.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> and gate <math id="A8.T13.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=1</annotation></semantics></math> selected on the validation split</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.2.13" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A8.T13.2.13.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;" colspan="3"><em id="A8.T13.2.13.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Optimisation of the base policy</em></td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.2.14" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A8.T13.2.14.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">Data</td>
<td id="A8.T13.2.14.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">–</td>
<td id="A8.T13.2.14.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">
<span id="A8.T13.2.14.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:210.6pt;">
<span id="A8.T13.2.14.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">AndroidControl training split as cached, 13,594 of 13,604 episodes / 74,714 of 74,722 steps (<a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Protocol details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>); cached frozen features; candidates capped at 80 per step</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A8.T13.2.15" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A8.T13.2.15.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">Loss</td>
<td id="A8.T13.2.15.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">–</td>

</span></td></tr>

</span></td></tr>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 13: </span><span id="A8.T13.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Components and hyperparameters of GUI-JEPA.</span> Parameter counts are measured. The encoder and the CLIP text encoder are frozen and their outputs cached before policy training; the span ranker and the click reranker are trained after the base policy with the base policy fixed.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A8.T13" title="In Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> lists every component with its measured parameter count and the settings of the reported models; the paragraphs below add only what the table does not state.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Encoder.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The encoder is the ViT-L/16 of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dosovitskiy et al. (2021)</a></cite> from the timm library. Where I-JEPA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Assran et al., 2023</a>)</cite> uses multi-block masks, our student sees the screenshot with a random half of its patches zeroed and regresses the tokens that the EMA target computes on the full image at the masked positions. The encoder is frozen and its 196 patch tokens per frame are cached; the policy never updates it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Predictor, head and matcher.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All candidates of a step form one predictor batch. The residual form was chosen in IDD pilots without the text matcher: a predictor that re-synthesises the whole latent erases local detail, lowering AC-Low click grounding to 34.8 against 46.8 for the identity map, and the residual form raises pilot AC-Low from 40.59 to 43.93. At pilot scale (IDD) the structural head’s constraint, that its only candidate-dependent visual input is the candidate-conditioned latent, decides whether the pathway is used: a concat-MLP head over <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\mathbf{z}_{t},\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c},\mathrm{cand}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>cand</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\mathbf{z}_{t},\tilde{\mathbf{z}}_{t}^{c},\mathrm{cand}]</annotation></semantics></math> ignores the predictor (within 1.4 AC-Low points), while the structural head gains 8.8 points (<a href="#S4.F4" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>b; <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Design alternatives not adopted ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>). The conditioning vector uses the frozen CLIP text embedding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Radford et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. The MiniLM-L12 text matcher <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Reimers and Gurevych, 2019</a>)</cite> carries most of the click grounding: in the pilot, grounding rose from 37.4 to 70.2 when it was added. The <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> argument is copied as a goal span, which can be correct on at most 81.6% of IDD <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training skips the 1.6% of training click steps whose ground-truth element is not enumerated. Neither text ranker changes the action-type decision of the base policy, but both act in AC-Low as well as AC-High (<a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Per-subsplit waterfall ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 14: </span><span id="A8.T14.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Same-protocol comparison with a 7B VLM agent on AC-High (IDD).</span> All systems see the same screenshots, enumerated candidates and ground-truth history and are scored with the same step-accuracy rules. The click rows use the 2,379 click and long-press steps whose ground-truth element is enumerated: <em id="A8.T14.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">type recall</em> is the share predicted as a click, <em id="A8.T14.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">grounding (all)</em> the share answered correctly with type errors counted as misses, and <em id="A8.T14.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">grounding <math id="A8.T14.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mid" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∣</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mid</annotation></semantics></math> type</em> the share correct among the steps predicted as a click. ms/step: median over the 100 real IDD steps timed for all systems (<a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>). Ours: seed 3, reported in the main text, and the mean <math id="A8.T14.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> sd over three seeds.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Same-protocol 7B reference.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> (8.29B parameters, measured) is fine-tuned with LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> on 4,000 of the 13,594 cached training episodes for one epoch, with one adapter per setting (3.5 / 4.4 GPU-h for High / Low on one H20); the AC-Low adapter’s prompt adds the step instruction to the goal and shares every other setting, whereas GUI-JEPA serves both settings with one model. It is prompted with the same screenshot (377 image tokens; at most 384 visual tokens), the same enumerated candidate list and the same ground-truth history as GUI-JEPA, decodes a JSON action greedily, and is scored by the byte-identical judge on the same 716 IDD episodes. Beyond <a href="#A8.T14" title="In Training. ‣ Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>, the High adapter reaches a click top-5 recall of 95.3, and the AC-Low adapter reaches 91.01 Low with type accuracy 97.4 (GUI-JEPA: 84.06, 92.4% of it). We report click grounding in two forms because the conditional form alone rewards predicting fewer clicks: our seed with the lowest type accuracy (74.9) has the highest conditional grounding (76.1). The 7B agent leads on every action type of <a href="#A8.T14" title="In Training. ‣ Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> except <span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wait</span>; <a href="#A8.T15" title="In Same-protocol 7B reference. ‣ Appendix H Implementation details and hyperparameters ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> converts the per-type differences into contributions to the overall gap. The fine-tuned number is close to published 7B SFT results on AndroidControl (69.7–71.2 High for Qwen2-VL-7B and OS-Atlas-7B fine-tuned on AndroidControl, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025</a>, Tab. 5</cite>), which use the OS-Atlas judge on 7,708 test samples; under our judge and split it serves as the same-protocol reference.</p>
</div>

<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Latency measurement details</h2>

<figure id="A9.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.36877v1/fig_latency_sweep.svg" id="A9.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/362;" width="476" height="362"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span><span id="A9.F8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Same-hardware per-step latency</span> (median, one H20, batch 1). Stars: the deployed GUI-JEPA pipeline on the 100 real AC-High IDD steps timed for both systems, placed at their median of 28 scored actions (18 a11y candidates plus global actions). Lines: the synthetic fixed-<math id="A9.F8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> micro-benchmark with random inputs and <math id="A9.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> scored actions (<a href="#A9.T16" title="In Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>), a scaling illustration only. Horizontal lines: the same-protocol Qwen2.5-VL-7B SFT agent (merged LoRA) on the same steps with vLLM and HF transformers. Measurement boundaries: see the common protocol in the text.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 16: </span><span id="A9.T16.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Real-step serving path of the deployed GUI-JEPA pipeline and the synthetic micro-benchmark</span> (one NVIDIA H20, batch 1). Real-step rows: the deployed pipeline, timed end to end on real AC-High IDD test steps; “shared 100” are the steps on which the 7B agent was also timed (identical screenshots, candidates and history), a subset of the “all 200” steps timed for GUI-JEPA. Ratios use the shared 100 steps only, against the same-protocol 7B SFT agent (merged LoRA) timed end to end: 206.7 ms with vLLM (<math id="A9.T16.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math>16 GB peak memory) and 506.7 ms with HF transformers (15.9 GB). Synthetic rows: random image tensors and candidate vectors at a fixed number <math id="A9.T16.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> of scored actions, 100-iteration median, a scaling illustration only. Measurement boundaries: see the common protocol below.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span><span id="A9.F9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Latency decomposition in the synthetic fixed-<math id="A9.F9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> micro-benchmark</span> (one NVIDIA H20, batch 1, fp32 eager, <math id="A9.F9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>57</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}57</annotation></semantics></math> scored actions, random image tensors and candidate vectors, 100-iteration median). The click-reranker segment is amortised over the action mix; a click step takes 98.4 ms. The benchmark excludes JPEG decoding, CPU ROI pooling and the span ranker and is a scaling illustration only; real-step medians are in <a href="#A9.T16" title="In Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Common protocol.</h4>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All latencies are measured on one NVIDIA H20 at batch 1 with a single request and no concurrent load on the GPU, with CUDA synchronisation before and after each timed step, and reported as medians. GUI-JEPA timing includes JPEG decoding and CPU candidate and ROI preparation, and 7B timing includes image preprocessing and tokenisation; screenshot capture, accessibility-tree retrieval and parsing, and action execution on the device are excluded for every system. Every latency and speed ratio in the main text comes from the 100 real IDD steps on which both systems were timed (<a href="#S4.T3" title="In 4.5 Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and <a href="#A9.T16" title="Table 16 ‣ Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>). The 200-step medians include steps the 7B agent never ran and are given for reference only.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">7B agent on real steps.</h4>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent is timed on the first 110 AC-High IDD test steps in test-set order (10 warm-up, 100 measured) with the prompt of its accuracy evaluation: the screenshot at a 377-token image budget, the goal, the ground-truth history and the enumerated candidate list in the Qwen chat template, 931 input tokens on average. It decodes greedily until the end-of-sequence token and emits 11.75 new tokens on average, its most favourable configuration. End to end, including CPU prompt preparation (chat template, image processor, tokenisation), HF transformers 4.57 in bf16 with flash-attention 2 needs 506.7 ms per step for the merged LoRA-SFT model (generation alone 499.1 ms; prefill 189 ms, decode 28.3 ms per token), 504.6 ms for the zero-shot base model (p90 580.6; prefill 187 ms, 27.5 ms per token; 15.9 GB peak) and 753.6 ms for the unmerged LoRA model used in the accuracy evaluation (p90 889.3; prefill 229 ms, 47.8 ms per token; 16.2 GB). Merging is the deployment configuration, so our ratios use the merged model. With vLLM 0.11.2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite> in bf16 the merged model needs 206.7 ms end to end (generation alone 206.5 ms; prefill 96 ms, 10.2 ms per token) with prefix caching off, and 211.9 ms (p90 250) with prefix caching on, where the 15 ms prefill and 18.5 ms per token reflect the cached system prefix.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">GUI-JEPA real-step serving path.</h4>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We time the final pipeline end to end on the first 210 AC-High IDD test steps in test-set order (10 warm-up, 200 measured, 46 episodes), so the 7B agent’s 100 measured steps are a subset of ours. Each step executes the full pipeline, with the span ranker only on steps predicted as <span id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> (10% of steps) and the click reranker only on steps predicted as click (63.5%). The 200 steps have 24.4 a11y candidates on average (median 18, p90 49) and 33.0 scored actions (median 28.5, p90 58). The served policy is the evaluated policy: its base-policy action matches the offline evaluation, which uses precomputed encoder features, on 198 of the 200 steps (99.0%), and on all 200 when both receive the same preprocessed frames. On the 200 steps the bf16 and fp32 pipelines make identical predictions, including the typed text. On all IDD steps, the base policy (base stage of <a href="#S4.T2" title="In 4.4 Gains from the two text rankers ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) changes by <math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.18</annotation></semantics></math> Low / <math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.07" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.07</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.07</annotation></semantics></math> High in bf16 relative to fp32, with 99.8% step-level agreement on type, candidate and direction. The typed string agrees on 151 of the 322 High steps where both predict <span id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span>; that ranker is rarely right in High, and High <span id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">input_text</span> accuracy moves from 15.6 to 14.2 (4 of 282 steps).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Where the GUI-JEPA step time goes.</h4>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Over the 200 steps, the fp32 p50 decomposes into 8.3 ms JPEG decoding and resizing (9.6% of the mean), 11.4 ms ViT-L (13.0%), 1.2 ms candidate construction, 1.2 ms ROI encoding, 39.7 ms predictor and structural head (51.4%), 8.8 ms matcher (12.7%), 8.1 ms click reranker when it fires (6.8%) and 21.5 ms span ranker when it fires (3.3%); in bf16 the p50 components are 7.0 ms decoding, 7.7 ms ViT-L, 11.8 ms predictor and head and 10.4 ms matcher. By a11y candidate count the fp32 p50 is 58.9 ms below 15 candidates, 74.5 at 15–29, 125.1 at 30–59 and 168.7 at 60 or more. The CLIP goal embedding runs once per episode and is not included: its median is 5.6 ms (mean 10.8 ms, raised by one 245 ms first call), about 1.3 ms per step amortised at the median and 2.4 ms at the mean. In AC-Low the step instruction changes at every step, so the CLIP call recurs per step; all real-step timings are AC-High.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A9.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.36877v1/fig_qual.png" id="A9.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/161;" width="476" height="161" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span><span id="A9.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Complementary errors behind the cascade</span> on two real AC-High IDD steps (GUI-JEPA with both rankers and the same-protocol 7B SFT agent, given the same candidates). (a) GUI-JEPA is right with a margin above the 50%-coverage threshold <math id="A9.F10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> (the median margin), so the cascade keeps its answer, while the 7B agent presses the wrong key. (b) GUI-JEPA picks the wrong destination with a margin below <math id="A9.F10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, so the cascade escalates the step to the 7B agent, which is right. Boxes: ground truth (green), GUI-JEPA (purple), 7B (rose).</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A9.F11" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.36877v1/fig_routing.svg" id="A9.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/275;" width="476" height="275"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 11: </span><span id="A9.F11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GUI-JEPA as the cheap first stage of a cascade</span> (AC-High, IDD). Steps with a large top-two margin are answered by GUI-JEPA, the rest by the 7B SFT agent; labels: share of steps kept by GUI-JEPA. Latency: the mean GUI-JEPA step plus, on escalated steps, the mean vLLM 7B step (same 100 real steps).</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">GUI-JEPA synthetic fixed-<math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> micro-benchmark.</h4>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The synthetic rows of <a href="#A9.T16" title="In Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> and the lines of <a href="#A9.F8" title="In Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> time the final pipeline in eager PyTorch on a random 224-px image tensor with random action and ROI vectors and dummy candidate texts and bounds, 100-iteration median. <math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> counts the scored actions in the predictor batch, that is, a11y candidates plus global actions. <math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}23</annotation></semantics></math> and 57 equal the mean and p95 a11y candidate counts of IDD, but a real step scores more actions than it has a11y candidates (33.0 against 24.4 on average on the timed steps), so the synthetic <math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}23</annotation></semantics></math> point understates a typical step and the real-step rows are the operating point. The encoder cost is fixed, and the predictor batch grows by about 1.2 ms per scored action in fp32 and 0.37 ms in bf16; <span id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span> on top of bf16 lowers the bf16 times by a further 0.7–6.6%. The benchmark’s inputs are not real screenshots, so it only shows the linear scaling in <math id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Literature latencies.</h4>

<div id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">8B-class GUI agents average 2.6–10.6 s per step in a live-device benchmark (<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sui et al., 2026</a>, Tab. 2</cite>; means over valid sessions, BF16 on H20 GPUs with the GPU count and serving engine not stated, each model under its official inference protocol where one is released). V-Droid reports 0.7 s per decision, covering all candidates of a step (0.44 s batched prefill verification plus 0.30 s action completion), and 4.3 s per step end to end, 3.03 s of it in a GPT-4 working-memory update (verifier on two RTX 4090 GPUs; <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2026</a></cite>). Neither shares our measurement boundary or statistic (means over live-device sessions with model-specific prompts and outputs, against our median over 100 real test steps).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Confidence routing to the 7B agent</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GUI-JEPA and the same-protocol 7B agent err on different steps (<a href="#A9.F10" title="In Where the GUI-JEPA step time goes. ‣ Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>): on IDD AC-High at least one of them is right on 78.9% of steps on average over the three GUI-JEPA seeds (78.7–79.2), against 70.87 for the 7B agent and 60.12 for GUI-JEPA. We therefore test GUI-JEPA as the cheap first stage of a cascade: a step is answered by GUI-JEPA when the margin between its top two final scores is at least <math id="A10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> and escalated to the 7B SFT agent otherwise. The margin predicts whether GUI-JEPA is correct with AUROC 0.74–0.77, and on its most confident half of the steps GUI-JEPA alone is 77.6–79.2% accurate. Setting <math id="A10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> at coverage quantiles (the share of steps kept by GUI-JEPA) traces the curve of <a href="#A9.F11" title="In Where the GUI-JEPA step time goes. ‣ Appendix I Latency measurement details ‣ GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latentsas a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> (main-text model). At 50% coverage the cascade reaches 69.48 High on average over seeds, 98% of the 7B agent’s 70.87, at 0.91<math id="A10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> its mean vLLM latency with fp32 GUI-JEPA and 0.76<math id="A10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> with bf16 (with HF serving, <math id="A10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.9+0.5\times 515.7\approx 345" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>86.9</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>515.7</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>345</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.9+0.5\times 515.7\approx 345</annotation></semantics></math> ms against 515.7 ms, 0.67<math id="A10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>). Because <math id="A10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is set on coverage quantiles of the same IDD steps, we report the cascade as a deployment mode. For the main-text model the margin AUROC is 0.74, at least one system is right on 78.7% of steps, and the 50%-coverage cascade reaches 69.67 (98% of 70.87) at the same expected latency, with GUI-JEPA 78.1% accurate on the steps it keeps.</p>
</div>
</section>
</article>
